title: Fresh EEG Neural-Effect Gate
claim_target: bounded within_person causal pre_keypress EEG sensor_signal advantage for performed hand and performed key prediction
scientific_claim_ceiling: A future clean execution may establish only a bounded within-person pre-keypress EEG sensor-signal effect for performed-hand or performed-key prediction on the exact qualified S20 overt-typing block. It cannot establish brain-specific origin, intended-thought decoding, continuous event detection, unseen-person or session generalization, real-time operation, portable hardware, home use, or clinical utility.

primary_source_findings.finding: The published EEG system used 61 EEG and three ocular channels at 1 kHz, and the decoder used known keypress-aligned 500 ms windows from -200 to +300 ms. Hand and key classification peaked after keypress, and the authors state the system is not real time and depends on known keystroke onsets.

The published preprocessing distinguishes the key actually pressed from the intended target key and usually analyzes the intended target. Typing errors alter interkey timing and reduce decoding performance, so performed action and intended text are noninterchangeable estimands.

EEGNet uses depthwise and separable convolutions to build a compact EEG-specific temporal and spatial classifier across multiple BCI paradigms. This supports a small candidate family but does not validate it on S20.
The Same Analysis Approach recommends applying the main pipeline to design variables, simulated confounds, null data, and controls so analysis-specific failures remain visible.
Label and restricted feature permutations answer different classifier questions. Event-window corruption controls are falsification probes, not interchangeable perfect neural nulls.
Small predictive neuroimaging samples have large error bars that fold-wise variation can underestimate. Keypress windows do not create independent trials or additional biological replicates.

current_warnings: The expected 61 EEG plus three ocular channels 1 kHz and 64 trials are cohort or protocol facts, not verified S20 file evidence.
The published -200 to +300 ms window includes post-keypress activity and cannot support a causal or real-time claim.
Known keypress timing and event count make the future task keypress aligned rather than continuous decoding.
Performed key and intended target are distinct; the primary Loop 55 target is the performed key.
One participant and one block cannot support population unseen-person session or device inference.
Missing ocular muscular motion gaze audio or other peripheral measurements narrow the claim ceiling even if sensor controls pass.
The Loop 48 tiny model family was negative on S21 and its synthetic repair missed absolute gates; it is not a proven EEG representation.
